title: Euler's Method: Tangent Steps Along a Slope Field
topic: Euler's explicit method — march along a slope field by taking small tangent steps. Each step uses the current derivative to estimate where the solution heads next. As step size h shrinks, the polyline hugs the true curve more closely; as it grows, error opens up like a fan.

beats.narration: How do you draw a curve when you only know its slope at every point? Walk it.
Here is a slope field for y prime equals f of t comma y. At every grid point a little tangent shows which way the solution heads.

elements.content: Grid of short tangent strokes in chalk-300
Tangents whisper which way to walk.

beats.narration: Pick a starting point. Step forward by a small amount h, following the tangent. From the new spot, read the new tangent, and step again.

elements.content: Euler steps as amber dots + line segments
Each step uses the local slope.

beats.narration: Make h bigger and the polyline starts to drift away from the true curve. The error fan opens because each tangent only knows the starting point of its step.

elements.content: Larger Euler steps in rose, drifting off the curve
Error gap arrows between rose path and violet truth

beats.narration: Euler's method trades exact for explicit. Smaller steps follow truer curves — at the cost of doing more work.
